tasks.title: Freeze the Common Crawl DEV candidates
tasks.goal: Use the public CC-MAIN-2025-43 Parquet index to freeze the dev.to candidate paths that meet the definition and select a capture location for each path.
inputs: Root configuration for the crawl, seed, transfer limits, and pilot.cc_records
The cc-index-table.paths.gz file and subset=warc Parquet index for the selected crawl
acceptance_criteria: The saved compressed list matches the SHA-256 in the manifest, and its eligible keys correspond one-to-one with the processed index ledger.
The five-candidate pilot records the index filters, normalized paths, and capture locations.
Candidate rows are unique and sorted by path. Recomputed IDs match every row, and capture locations follow the timestamp and tie-breaking rules.
Per-file counts agree with the totals. The report confirms processing of every index file and distinguishes the covered scope from historical reference counts.
steps: Freeze the list source, compression limit, filters, and candidate route definition. Verify the saved list hash before reusing it.
Read only the required columns and ranges in key order. Read back five candidates from the index first to verify deduplication and capture selection.
Commit the file counts and candidates together. Continue within the configured limits until all keys in the saved list have been processed.
Write the candidate list with the earliest capture frozen for each path. Have an independent reviewer verify file completion, candidate IDs and paths, and counts from the saved artifacts.
pitfalls: HTTP 200 and HTML are index acquisition filters. Assess the article body, publication year, and English-language eligibility later.
Report partial index counts as partial. Leave counts for unprocessed keys missing.
tasks.resume_instructions: On interruption, record the manifest.paths.gz hash and the first unprocessed key. When complete, hand candidates.jsonl and manifest.json to D02.

tasks.title: Save Common Crawl WARC records and raw HTML
tasks.goal: For every candidate frozen in D01, retrieve the specified WARC byte range and save the original HTML bytes and acquisition outcome.
inputs: The output_dir of the completed D01 attempt in the same run_id
D01 candidates and the manifest hash
Root configuration for the seed, transfer limits, and pilot.cc_records
acceptance_criteria: The ledger has exactly one row per D01 candidate in the frozen order. Final rows are marked succeeded or failed with a reason.
The first five records have documented checks for range retrieval, compression, and saving and reading back the original HTML.

For each success, the input location, received length, WARC URL, type, internal HTTP 200, and HTML and WARC hashes can be verified. Publication, crawl, and save timestamps are stored in separate fields.
The ledger retains failure reasons, attempt history, retry limits, and wait deadlines. An independent reviewer checks total counts and hashes of saved files.
steps: Verify the frozen D01 artifacts and use the seed to order all candidates. Use the same candidate IDs in filenames.
Try the first five records and verify HTTP 206, the received length, and WARC and HTML validation and storage.
Retrieve pending candidates one at a time. Request the data, save the WARC, save the HTML, then update the ledger. Resume at the next unfinished chunk.

Process retries within their limits and wait deadlines. Finalize outcomes for all candidates, retaining failures. Report success counts and a breakdown of failures, and check the raw data against the ledger.
pitfalls: Record the range response's HTTP 206 and the archived page's HTTP 200 separately.
WARC-Date records the crawl timestamp. Keep the publication timestamp from the original page and the retrieval timestamp.
Keep failed outcomes in the original candidate set. Use the designated capture for each candidate.
tasks.resume_instructions: Before resuming, check not_before and the unprocessed ordinal. Hand the evidence of successful acquisitions and all rows, including failures, to Phase 1 T00.

tasks.title: Retrieve a fixed DEV API sample for January through October 2026
tasks.goal: Freeze 1,000 candidate IDs per UTC month for a total of 10,000 and save the raw JSON and acquisition outcomes from the public API.
inputs: DEV API listing and detail responses
UTC interval from 2026-01-01 inclusive to 2026-11-01 exclusive
Root configuration for the seed, monthly count, and transfer limits
acceptance_criteria: The connection probe records five results. The listing page number and oldest row establish that the scan reached the lower date bound. Saved listing pages are consecutive from page 1, and the report describes the limitations of offset pagination.

The plan can be reproduced from the seeded hash order and contains 1,000 unique IDs per UTC month from January through October, for 10,000 in total. Selection uses the full eligible set regardless of tags or language attributes.
The first five planned responses have been saved and read back. Every planned ID has a saved, empty, not_found, or failed outcome. All original planned IDs are accounted for.

Valid HTTP 200 detail responses are saved, including empty bodies, with verifiable response IDs and hashes. Failures carry reasons. An independent reviewer verifies the monthly breakdown and checks the raw JSON for credentials.
steps: Retrieve one listing page and verify the format and storage of five API detail responses. Use the fixed HTTPS host and keep authorized credentials in memory only.
Commit listing pages in page-number order, convert timestamps to UTC, and collect in-window IDs by month. Keep a record of duplicates, discrepancies, and evidence of reaching the lower date bound.

Verify that the scan reached the lower bound and that each month has enough candidates. Select 1,000 IDs per month in seeded hash order. Cycle through the months from January to October to assign fixed plan positions.
After retrieving and checking the first five planned detail responses, process the rest in chunks. Observe the budget and wait deadlines and reuse saved raw JSON.
Reconcile retrieval outcomes for every ID and the monthly counts before eligibility screening. Freeze the ledger and raw JSON hashes and record the verification and handoff.
pitfalls: Reaching the lower date bound through offset pages leaves overall listing coverage unknown.
The API body reflects the article at retrieval time. Record HTTP 200, body availability, and English-language eligibility as distinct outcomes.
Keep the original monthly quotas and IDs even when a month is short or an ID fails.
tasks.resume_instructions: During listing, record the next page. After freezing the plan, record the next unprocessed ID. Once complete, pass plan.jsonl and responses.jsonl to the Phase 2 corpus task.

tasks.title: Freeze the inputs and execution conditions
tasks.goal: Freeze the candidate set, source HTML, extraction rules, and execution environment, then create an extraction ledger for all candidates.
inputs: D02 acquisitions.jsonl, manifest, summary, verification, and HTML for successful rows
acceptance_criteria: Candidate IDs are unique, and all acquisition states and HTML hashes match D02.
The five-candidate probe and synthetic negative cases distinguish acquisition failures, extraction failures, and empty S.
Every candidate has an extraction state, and all exclusions are accounted for. SHA-256 hashes for the code, environment, and configuration can be verified again.
steps: Connect to the accepted D02 attempt in read-only mode. Copy candidate IDs, URLs, dates, HTML references, and sources into the ledger.
Freeze the bundled extractor as extract.py. Record Python, lxml, libxml, locale and UTC settings, and dependency installation instructions.
Run a small extraction on the five fixed D02 candidates. Independently check the body selector and its correspondence to the source HTML.
Apply the same code to every candidate. Record success, acquisition failure, missing or ambiguous body, and decoding or parsing failure. Keep empty S among the successful extractions.
Use an independent implementation to check input and shard SHA-256 hashes, uniqueness, the ID set, and edge cases.
pitfalls: Use the current run's criteria for inclusion independently of historic counts and run IDs.
Keep a row for every failed candidate.
Leave attempts that stop after five candidates in progress.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the full candidate ledger, extraction results, probe, and code hashes to T01. Reuse matching shards when resuming partway through.

tasks.title: Body language classification and English cohort
tasks.goal: Assign a status to every candidate and freeze the analysis cohort based on English body text and UTC publication year.
inputs: T00 extraction.jsonl, input-ledger.csv, pilot.json, and original D02 sources
acceptance_criteria: There is exactly one language and inclusion row per candidate. UTC boundaries and counts for all states reconcile.
Blinded calibration, validation, and diagnostics are separate. The freeze order, sample shortfalls, and evidence for manual overrides are saved.
The cohort excludes non-English, indeterminate, and out-of-period articles and retains short and identical articles.
steps: Freeze the bundled language_rules.py as language-rules.py and lock all 75 Lingua languages. Use T00 probe articles to verify that S, P, L, and 1,200-character spans can be saved and read back.
Select 20 calibration and 10 validation examples per year and a separate diagnostic sample by hash. Use calibration and diagnostics to check quality when freezing the 0.70 and 0.30 thresholds.
Score every candidate automatically. Store manual overrides in a separate column only for evidence-backed full-text decisions from calibration or diagnostics. Save the blinded validation results.
Set adopted=true only for English candidates with a UTC publication year from 2018 through 2025. Retain rows that are out of scope, missing a timestamp, mixed, empty, or unavailable.
Independently recalculate candidate hashes, complete S span coverage and labels, UTC years, and sample and inclusion totals.
pitfalls: Use html lang, CC language, and tags as hints only.
Keep English-dominant mixed articles as candidates only.
Evaluate the validation group independently of manual overrides.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass cohort.csv and hashes of the frozen extraction and language evidence to T02. Record insufficient support with its evidence.

tasks.title: Segmentation, features, and metadata
tasks.goal: Measure words, sentences, bold spans, headings, and metadata from the same body projection, and freeze the six primary metrics and secondary metrics.
inputs: T01 cohort.csv and language-review
T00 extraction.jsonl and frozen extract.py
HTML archived by D02
acceptance_criteria: Each included article has one article row, one metadata row, and six primary metric rows.
S=P+L+U, sentence and word offsets, bold deduplication and denominators, and known author IDs agree with an independent reading.
Checks cover synthetic examples, fixed samples, and the evidence for v2 metadata. They distinguish zero, NA, no use, and projection failure.
Downstream tasks can reuse the frozen code, fixtures, and data schema.
steps: Save the bundled segmentation.py and frozen controls. Project P/L/U units, owning blocks, sentences, and words using Unicode offsets.

Test the included articles from the five candidates and supplement any shortfall with synthetic fixtures. Read the fixed sample with years hidden to diagnose sentence boundaries, words, and evidence for organizations and authors.

Reconcile source DOM order with S words for every included article whose SHA-256 hash has been verified. Save H, bold spans, lists, code positions, the six primary metrics, and secondary metrics such as MATTR.
Use the t02_metadata_v2.py rules to save single numeric authors, tags, organizations, article-type cues, and sources. Freeze t02-strata-map.json as topic-map.json.
Use independent verification to reconstruct the ID set, token types, half-open owner-to-source ranges, M01–M06, bold and link positions, metadata conflicts, and NA reasons.
pitfalls: Use the full S scope for S measures.
Treat organization handles and author IDs as distinct identifiers.
Keep inline code outside the S word stream.
Limit each structure projection failure to its affected metrics.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the cohort, articles, metrics, metadata, topic map, frozen segmentation.py, and fixtures to T03.

tasks.title: Cohort statistics and coverage
tasks.goal: Produce tables and figures that show candidate counts, valid coverage, missing data, and distributions.
inputs: T00 input and extraction ledgers
T01 cohort.csv
T02 articles, metrics, and metadata
acceptance_criteria: Article counts reconcile from candidacy to inclusion. P/L/U/S word counts, bands, and quantiles can be recalculated.
Coverage states for eight years, 96 months, and 32 quarters identify partial years explicitly.
Year and period counts distinguish unknown dates, known authors, organizations, tags, and duplicate text.
steps: Join dates, acquisition state, language state, and inclusion decisions for every candidate. Check for missing and duplicate rows.

For included articles, aggregate P/L/U/S totals, medians, quantiles, and word-count bands including zero. Summarize date availability and denominators for identical text, authors, tags, and organizations.
Build complete grids for UTC months and quarters. Use settings and acquisition evidence to classify them as complete, partial, unobserved, or unknown.
Open the figure files and independently check points, yearly denominators, and NA values against the source tables.
pitfalls: Keep unobserved months in 2025 distinct from months with zero articles.
Describe counts as counts for the archived cohort.
Derive publication years from publication dates.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the cohort table, dates, coverage, and identical included ID set to A01–A08.

tasks.title: Article and Paragraph Length
tasks.goal: Compare P and S word counts and paragraph lengths, and produce the primary M01 comparison.
inputs: T03 coverage and cohort
T02 articles, metadata, and M01
T00 extraction results and original HTML for the fixed sample
acceptance_criteria: The equally year-weighted M01 difference on the log1p scale, raw word counts, all-article point estimate, and author-cluster interval can be reproduced.
The article-weighted and paragraph-weighted paragraph distributions are reported separately.
The selection rule and audit results for long articles are recorded, and zero words and NA are distinguishable.
steps: Compute annual P and S word count distributions and bands, the January–September supplementary results, and the M01 point estimates for all articles and for known authors, along with the author-cluster interval.
Calculate the median length of P paragraph owners and construct distributions that weight paragraphs equally and articles equally.
Audit the prespecified longest-article candidates for each year against the original HTML.
Use separate formulas to check the year weights, log scale, interval replicates, and figure.
pitfalls: Interpret raw word counts and differences on the log scale as distinct quantities for M01.
Use paragraph data to draw conclusions about paragraph length.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the M01 cohort, original measurement scale, year weights, and long-article audit to V01 and R01.

tasks.title: Sentence Rhythm and Punctuation
tasks.goal: Compare M02–M04 and the secondary measures while retaining the sentence-count and punctuation denominators.
inputs: T03 cohort and coverage
T02 P owner blocks, sentences, tokens, and M02–M04
acceptance_criteria: M02–M04 are calculated from the fixed P data, with distinct cases for zero words, a single sentence, and low n.
Sentence-based comma intervals and the legacy article-level approximation are in separate columns. Commas within numbers are excluded.
The author-cluster intervals and figure can be independently verified from the inputs.
steps: Count mechanically segmented sentences, sentence lengths and fragments, differences between adjacent sentences, the share of single-sentence paragraphs, and punctuation.
Save the equally year-weighted differences in the primary metrics, the author-cluster intervals, and any annual shortfalls.
Calculate sentence-based comma intervals, the supplementary result for articles with at least five commas, and the legacy approximation separately.
Diagnose low sentence counts, extreme CV values, and candidate untagged code. Check negative cases and aggregates with an independent calculation.
pitfalls: Report sentence-length CV as NA for a single sentence.
Treat burstiness as a transformation of CV.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the sentence-length scales, metric-specific cohorts, and boundary issues to A10, A12, V01, and R01.

tasks.title: Lists, Bold Text, and Headings
tasks.goal: Compare how often articles use structural elements, how extensively they use them, and where they appear in S.
inputs: T03 cohort and coverage
T02 articles, DOM events, bold text, and M05/M06
acceptance_criteria: The equally year-weighted estimates and intervals for M05/M06, structural presence, and conditional intensity can be recalculated.
Counts of S words, L words, bold words, and bold spans agree for each region.
Empty regions, S=0, absent structures, projection failures, and the role of illustrative examples are distinguishable.
steps: Calculate primary M05/M06, the presence and amount of structural elements, and heading density and candidates.
Save counts for each half and each 20/60/20 region using the original S word ranks.
Select quality-check candidates by the fixed rule and compare them with the raw and cleaned DOM.
Independently reconstruct positions, denominators, primary contrasts, intervals, and the figure.
pitfalls: Record zero when there is no list and the S word count is positive. Record NA when there are no S words.
Track bold spans and bold words separately, and distinguish DOM lists from the presence of L words.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the primary contrasts, positional ranges, and projection limits to A09, A12, V01, and R01.

tasks.title: Vocabulary Discovery and Validation
tasks.goal: Validate changes in the fixed candidate phrases across periods, keeping authors and exact P duplicates on one side of the split.
inputs: T03 cohort
T02 original P sentences, owner units, tokens, L/H, MATTR, and metadata
acceptance_criteria: Known authors and exact nonempty P hashes have zero overlap between the discovery and validation splits.
The candidate hash is frozen before validation results are opened, and every selection decision and failure to replicate is retained.
An independent implementation can check original units, sentence and nonword boundaries, the denominator for zero-word P, rarity decisions, watch terms, and insufficient MATTR windows.
steps: Build connected components from nonempty P hashes and known authors, and split the components by a fixed-seed hash.
Count all one- to five-word candidates in the discovery split according to the bundled rules. Freeze lists of increases, decreases, previously rare terms, and prespecified watch terms.
Open the validation split and calculate differences, ratios, directions, threshold attainment, and component-cluster intervals for each candidate. Keep P, L, and H and the two splits separate.
Save results on author coverage, topic and word-count bands, annual MATTR, and the limitations of edit timestamps and inline code boundaries.
Independently check for leakage and verify selection ranks, denominators, word boundaries, and validation rows.
pitfalls: Report agreement in the direction of point estimates separately from statistical significance.
Keep the prespecified thresholds when fewer candidates qualify.
Limit the exact-duplicate conclusion to exact P matches.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass split assignments and components from `split.csv` to A06 and V01. Pass the validation table, failures to replicate, and boundary risks to A09 and R01.

tasks.title: Author Voice and Direct Address
tasks.goal: Measure pronouns, contractions, connective expressions, and punctuation in P using a dictionary.
inputs: T03 cohort
T02 P units, sentences, tokens, and author IDs
acceptance_criteria: Word-form counts for all articles, the share of articles using each form, and density denominators for all articles and articles using the form are reported separately.
Ambiguous pronouns and contractions are checked in blinded excerpts, and the dictionary is frozen before results are examined.
First-person singular and contraction rates per 1,000 P words can be mapped unambiguously to T02 IDs.
steps: Freeze the bundled dictionary and scan P for word forms and phrases, including paragraph openings.
Summarize the share of articles using each form, density per 1,000 P words, conditional density, and zero-word status by year, period, and word-count band.
Audit interpretations of US, we, you, quotations, and contractions against fixed excerpts.
Check dictionary matches, denominators, cluster resampling, and plotted values against an independent implementation.
pitfalls: Treat matches for I as word-form counts. Use content evidence to assess personal experience.
Interpret word-form matches as linguistic features. They provide no evidence of AI use on their own.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass word-form counts and denominators for the same articles to A07, and first-person singular and contraction densities to A12.

tasks.title: Headings, Openings, and Endings
tasks.goal: Compare dictionary-based heading functions, concentration of heading patterns, and expressions at article openings and endings.
inputs: T03 cohort
T02 headings and S/P positions
A04 split.csv and evidence that candidates were frozen
acceptance_criteria: The sequence of heading calibration, freezing, and evaluation is recorded, and heading absence, dictionary nonmatches, and concentration can be recalculated.
The presence of a summary, conditional section length, and S position each have an explicit denominator.
Opening and ending candidates are frozen before validation. All candidate results and checks for split leakage are verified.
steps: Calibrate the fixed heading dictionary on 60 blinded discovery candidates, then freeze the rules and record unmatched headings.
Calculate the S cursor and section word count for each heading, along with function sequences, annual concentration, and the size adjustment.
Use the first and last 50 P words in the A04 splits. Freeze 15 increasing and 15 decreasing two- to five-word sequences for each window, then validate them in the other split.
Independently verify original DOM order, heading hierarchy, concentration by identical text and author, fixed candidates, and the figure.
pitfalls: Assess full-article structural uniformity using evidence beyond the prevalence of summary headings.
Interpret dictionary labels as rule-based classifications.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass heading paths, span boundaries, and preceding S word counts to A11, and concentration and section lengths to R01.

tasks.title: Personal Experience and Concrete Verification Details
tasks.goal: Read content descriptions in a fixed blinded sample and examine how they correspond to automated proxies across all articles.
inputs: T03 cohort
T02 original DOM, sentence units, source article text, and metadata
A05 voice-article.csv
acceptance_criteria: The fixed calibration and evaluation samples are disjoint. Every evaluation article is read in full after the rules are frozen, and each article has an evidence-backed status and span.
The fixed subset is reevaluated in a separate session. The initial review, reevaluation, and adjudication are retained.
Corpus-wide proxies, sampled content, S and P denominators, indeterminate cases, and insufficient support are distinguishable.
steps: Order each year's articles by a fixed hash and save four for calibration and sixteen for evaluation. Hide year and author, then freeze the content rubric and proxy dictionary separately.

Select four evaluation articles per year and save a fixed packet for a separate session. Read every evaluation article in full and record evidence, S sentence IDs, status, content type, and operation mode for five categories.
Retain the unopened inputs, execution record, and adjudication for the separate-session reevaluation.
Measure all 25 proxies corpus-wide using fixed P phrase, number, link, and DOM rules. Check how A05 word forms correspond to content within the same sample.

Summarize upper and lower bounds, each denominator, article types, years, word-count bands, and proxy disagreements. Have another reader audit the evidence and check the counts with an independent implementation.
pitfalls: Distinguish whether the author did the work, whether the article reports it, and whether the proxy matches.
Keep indeterminate cases distinct from confirmed absence.
Record any missing reevaluation or unavailable detailed coding explicitly.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass fixed blinded calibration and evaluation packets and the crosswalk to A11. Pass separate proxy and content outputs to A09 and R01.

tasks.title: Code and Nearby Prose
tasks.goal: Measure the amount of code, language labels, and prose before and after code within a heading section.
inputs: T03 cohort
T00 extracted body_html
T02 S words, DOM events, and metadata
acceptance_criteria: Code blocks and inline code are counted once, and the original order, adjacent prose matches, and denominators for each status can be reconstructed.
The 12 fixed diagnostic cases are recorded, with zero, no match, and projection failure distinguishable.
Aggregates for all 22 metrics, intervals for the 12 specified metrics, and any strata with insufficient support are retained.
steps: Use 12 fixed examples to check pre, highlighted blocks, inline code, unknown language labels, adjacent code, and heading boundaries.
Save block and inline code counts and sizes, explicit classes, and statuses for all articles.
Match preceding and following prose within the same section, check it against the original S, and flag reused matches.
Apply the bundled aggregation and interval thresholds, then independently check the original HTML, denominators, positions, and figure.
pitfalls: Distinguish the presence of any code from the presence of a code block and keep the visible-character share separate from code characters per S word.
Preserve unknown language labels as unknown.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass code events and positions to A11 and denominators for each set to A09 and R01.

tasks.title: Changes in Topic and Author Composition
tasks.goal: Measure topic and length composition, weighting across known authors, and within-author differences.
inputs: T02 metrics, metadata, and articles
T03 coverage
A01–A08 comparisons and scopes of applicability
acceptance_criteria: For each metric, the six years of support, common support, fixed weights, effective sample size (ESS), and exclusion rates can be checked.
Unadjusted and fixed-composition estimates for the same cohort, equal known-author weighting, and within-author point differences and selection rates are distinguishable.
The decomposition identity, scope of each exploratory analysis, AI labels for tags and body phrases, and rules for unknown states can be verified.
steps: Freeze topic-by-P word-count cells that meet the support threshold of 30 and baseline weights q. Save cell, year, and classification keys for each metric.
Compare the full cohort with the common-support cohort, and compare fixed-composition estimates with unadjusted estimates for the same cohort.
Give each author equal weight within a year and calculate equally year-weighted within-author differences for authors observed in both periods.
Save the contribution decomposition, author-cluster intervals, and the scope of A04–A08. Use the fixed dictionary to label AI topics in tags and AI phrases in body S separately.
Recalculate the weights, decomposition, and intervals from the source tables, and independently verify the scopes of applicability.
pitfalls: An M01 comparison stratified by each article's own word-count band answers a separate question.
Limit conclusions to the cohort with sufficient support for the comparison.
Treat phrase presence as a text feature. AI use and semantic topics require their own evidence.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass `weights.csv` with `metric_id`, `topic_primary`, `W_P_band`, `q`, support, and baseline mass to A10. Pass composition and author comparisons to A12 and V01.

tasks.title: Timing of Changes
tasks.goal: After checking support, report the fixed boundary, placebo boundaries, exploratory breakpoints, and limits of extrapolation.
inputs: T03 coverage/date-ledger
T02 six main metrics and author IDs
A09 weights.csv, support, and cohort
acceptance_criteria: The grid for the full period, supported windows, reasons for insufficient support, seasonality, and the cohort and fixed-q masks can be reproduced.
Records cover the fixed boundary, pre-trend checks, both placebo boundaries, candidate BIC scores, and block-resampling statuses and failed replicate IDs.
Calendar-lag HAC, numerical results, plotted points, and stopping conditions are checked by independent calculation.
steps: Build annual, monthly, quarterly, and supplementary January–September grids and cohorts. Freeze support diagnostics before examining values.
Fit the prespecified regression with seasonality and actual calendar time t in supported windows. Verify the treatment of November and December 2022 and the calendar-lag HAC calculation.
Check pre-trends and the 2020 and 2021 placebo boundaries. Compare composition within the same months and retain rows with insufficient support.
Compare models with zero or one breakpoint across all candidate BIC scores, resample contiguous blocks, and apply the stability criteria.
Use synthetic data with missing observations and a complete example to independently verify coefficients, HAC, candidate masks, some or all replicates, and figures.
pitfalls: Treat a support table equivalent to S02 as a diagnostic. Estimation is a separate step.
Use calendar time so missing months remain visible in the time index.
Report supported timing for each metric individually. Counterfactual estimates and claims that AI caused the changes require a separate design.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass dates and period ranges, support, counterexamples to the conclusions, and cases with unavailable estimates to V01 and R01.

tasks.title: Position of the First Concrete Material
tasks.goal: Measure mechanically detected positions across all articles and locate the first title-relevant material in the fixed evaluation sample.
inputs: T02 mapping between S words and the DOM
A06 headings.csv
A07 fixed evaluation and calibration samples
A08 code-events.csv
acceptance_criteria: S cursor alignment agrees across all adopted articles. Positions are available for the four automated candidates, and zero, absence, missing input, and an undefined proportion are distinguishable.

Every article in the fixed A07 sample has a recorded title promise, an evidence span, and an out-of-S anchor or reason an assessment could not be made, as applicable. Separate-session reevaluation and adjudication are retained.
The correspondence between automated and content measures, sample sizes and support by stratum, counterexamples, and checks against the plotted values are recorded.
steps: Freeze the candidate dictionary and the title-relevance rubric using the calibration sample. Link A06/A08 DOM positions to S words and save the first mechanically detected occurrence for all articles.
Read A07 evaluation articles in full with the year hidden, and record the first material that addresses the title and the S and DOM spans that support it.
Reevaluate 32 prespecified articles in an independent top-level session, withholding the initial ratings, and adjudicate disagreements.
For each year pair in the fixed strata, require support of 30 for presence and 20 for position. Retain unsupported content comparisons.
Independently reread source text, recalculate positions, test negative cases for incorrect positions and S=0, and verify plotted values.
pitfalls: The historical run used 38,980 articles for automated measures and 128 for content review. Attribute findings to the applicable cohort.
Interpret earlier positions as positional measures. Reading time and quality require their own evidence.
Use a separate top-level session for reevaluation, with a different worker in the same conversation treated as part of the original session.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass separate automated and content tables, unsupported scopes, and counterexamples about absolute versus relative position to V01 and R01. Mark any outstanding reevaluation as required work.

tasks.title: Style Distances and Distributional Shifts
tasks.goal: Measure changes in the distributions of six metrics and distances from a fixed baseline for formatting and author voice.
inputs: T02 primary metrics, heading density, and P sentences
A05 grammatical person and contractions
A09 topic, P word-count band, and cohort tables
T03 coverage
acceptance_criteria: The equally year-weighted baseline CDF, quantiles, and ties can be reproduced.
Complete cases, common strata, fixed weights, and seeded different-author pair IDs and distances can be verified for each group.
Original scales, endpoint values, unknown categories, cohort coverage, equal author weighting, exact-text diagnostics, and pair dependence are documented.
steps: Calculate annual quantiles, zero-use shares, and the shares below, above, and exactly at baseline thresholds for the six metrics.
Compute fixed midranks from the baseline empirical CDF for complete cases. Account for each metric group, constant values, and missing values.
Measure common support for each group and stratum, then sample different-author pairs uniformly and summarize their distances.
Check a secondary sampling scheme that selects author pairs first, and diagnose exact matches among saved sentences shared between articles.
Use an independent implementation to check the baseline CDF, weights, selected pairs, denominators, and figure.
pitfalls: Account for dependence between pairs that share an article or author.
Report the two style distances individually as measures of formatting and voice.
Limit results for the unknown stratum to articles in that stratum.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass distribution results and separate formatting and voice findings, the scope of common strata, and limits on applicability to V01 and R01.

tasks.title: Sensitivity analyses
tasks.goal: Apply the prespecified sensitivity conditions one at a time to determine where the conclusions hold.
inputs: Accepted outputs from A01–A12
Frozen inputs and features from T00–T03
A04 duplicate-text components
acceptance_criteria: Every planned variant-by-primary-metric cell has a calculated value or a state with a reason. All required work has been processed.
Independent calculations verify differences from the original comparison, sample sizes, missingness, and support, and distinguish zeros by definition from reversals.
Unmeasured A04 boundaries and duplication, A11/A12 exploratory results, and figure counterexamples and constraints are saved.
steps: Freeze concrete variant IDs from the bundled condition list. Change one condition at a time.
Record comparisons for body regions, sentence boundaries, word forms, language, quality, topics, composition, authors, periods, dates, and duplicates.
Count zero support, insufficient support, and missing required inputs. Track implementation failures and pending work with separate states.
Independently check differences in scope between historical and current comparisons, A11/A12 exploratory analyses, and counterexamples.
Independently verify tables and figures and spot-check source articles for large deviations.
pitfalls: Record unevaluable cases explicitly.
Assess robustness using more than whether an interval crosses zero.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass all variant result states, counterexamples to apparent trends, and conditions that change the original scale or denominator to R01.

tasks.title: Japanese editorial materials
tasks.goal: Compile the comparisons and exploratory analyses into verified Japanese editorial materials and pass frozen inputs to Phase 2.
inputs: T03 cohort and coverage
Source tables, figures, manifests, and verification from A01–A12 and V01
Input assets from T00/T01/T02/A09
acceptance_criteria: The scales of the six primary metrics, source tables, point estimates for articles and known authors, interval populations, comparison years, and labels for tests left unrun all agree.
Claims and withheld conclusions can be traced to source table rows, denominators, counterexamples, and shortfalls. The existing figures were opened and checked.
Every required Phase 2 input resolves by package-relative path and hash, and all required issues have been resolved.
steps: Describe the cohort, primary comparisons, concrete material, positions, structure and style, counterexamples, and limitations in Japanese.
Verify the two metrics without a specified direction, the pre-result freeze time, the separate population for author-based intervals, and whether the p-value and Holm procedures ran.
Save the claim ledger and source table index, reasons for withholding claims, and limitations for each comparison cohort.
Open the figures and check that the values, sample sizes, periods, and intervals match the descriptions.
Register D02, the T00 extractor, T01 inclusion decisions and detector, T02 segmentation, metadata, and topic map, T03 coverage, and the A09 fixed q in phase2-inputs.json.
Have an independent reviewer check facts, measurements, figures, hashes, and relative references.
pitfalls: Base acceptance and withholding on this run's evidence. The original run recorded 22 accepted and four withheld claims.
Treat drafting the Japanese article, translating it into English, and publishing it as separate tasks.
Connect results across different cohorts only where the evidence supports the relationship.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the new run's outputs and the Phase 2 input index downstream. Synchronize and validate overall status with the CLI.

tasks.title: Lock the comparison and corpus intake plan
tasks.goal: Confirm the inputs and execution order for comparing the fixed UTC month windows across both acquisition routes.
inputs: R01's verified phase2-inputs.json and the files it indexes
D03's verified plan.jsonl, responses.jsonl, archived HTML, and raw responses
Fixed measurement specification and settings
acceptance_criteria: Check the R01 and D03 receipts, input paths, hashes, required columns, and join keys. List all inputs and exceptions.
Lock the primary cohort, all 60 year-month cells, weights, D/H, blinding, the order of comparisons, verification and reporting, and the definition version.
Record extraction and language pilot selection, access order, sample shortfalls, and differences from the full corpus.
steps: Open the output directories from the accepted R01 and D03 receipts. Verify required columns, normalized paths, counts, and ID mappings. Record UTC publication time, retrieval time, CC capture time, and edit time in separate fields.

Document differences in cohort scope and definitions from Phase 1. Lock the earlier inclusion decisions and use the common January through October UTC window for 2018–2022 and 2026 as the primary cohort.

Record the sequence and access restrictions in plan.json for corpus intake, inclusion decisions, specification lock, D candidate lock, H, independent recomputation, the 18 item decisions, and reporting. Distinguish valid zeros from missing measurements.

For the extraction pilot, use the first 50 items in the fixed plan as routine examples. Select up to two items each for code, tables, quotations, nested lists, embeds, cards, short text, warnings, empty bodies, Markdown-only bodies, and parse failures, ordered by SHA256(42:phase2-extraction:<category>:<article ID>). Keep duplicate IDs in a single row with all selection reasons.

For the language pilot, keep structural diagnostics separate from the accuracy sample. Use the first 50 items for calibration and the first five items per month in plan order for confirmation, excluding items already selected. Seal the labels before viewing the scores. Retain the original 50/19/50 counts as history.
pitfalls: The acquisition route and period overlap. Account for differences in coverage between the API and CC.
The pilot is a small quality check. Full-corpus inclusion decisions and comparisons require verification against every input.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the input index and plan to S02. On resumption, check the plan and input hashes against the original records.

tasks.title: Lock full-text inclusion decisions for the new corpus
tasks.goal: Record an outcome for every ID in the fixed plan and finalize the accepted English-language 2026 IDs and their extracted prose.
inputs: S01's input-index.json, plan.json, and pilot-plan.json
Indexed D03 raw responses, HTML, and Markdown
Indexed T00 extraction rules and T01 language rules
acceptance_criteria: Every plan ID appears once in records and once in decisions, in plan order. Counts by status sum to the total.
The English corpus matches the ledger's accept_english entries. Retain held items, missing prose, and unavailable responses in the ledger.
Trace text and evidence to the raw responses. Preserve proof that the corresponding scores were disclosed after the labels were sealed and retain the original decisions in the correction history.
Distinguish calibration, diagnostics, unused confirmation samples, and full-corpus review. Independently check actual extraction locations, joins, inclusion decisions, and provenance.
steps: Verify raw response IDs, UTC timestamps, and hashes in fixed plan order. Apply the earlier HTML extractor and save P/L/U, prose order, headings, bold spans, DOM mappings, and warnings. Record failures with reasons.
Run the fixed pilot. Keep items eligible when they fall into the structural diagnostic for text under 180 characters or have only Markdown. Avoid substituting Markdown without authorization.

Apply the earlier automated scoring rules to S, P, L, and 1,200-character sections of S. Review all S content independently of the scores and automated status. Reuse completed pilot rows after confirming identical text hashes. Process the remaining items in batches of up to 25.
Read the full text and seal the content labels and evidence. Then open only the corresponding scores. Index batch ranges, timestamps, reviewers, and hashes. Keep the thresholds fixed after review.

Hold mixed and uncertain results. Record non-English content, missing prose, and unavailable responses separately. Keep ads, short texts, and technical texts eligible. Append corrections with evidence, timestamp, the score disclosure flag, and the original record hash.

Independently check every inclusion decision and structure record and verify the join between the plan and raw responses. Report which inputs were reused and whether corpus intake and decisions were repeated.
pitfalls: The extracted S text and the complete original article have different language assessment scopes.
The original run's 8,942 acceptances, 220 holds, and 7 corrections are historical comparison figures.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the English-language IDs, records, reasons for non-inclusion, and input hashes to S03. Reuse verified sealed batches when resuming.

tasks.title: Lock the cohort, measurement specification, and author split
tasks.goal: Finalize the common months, fixed specification, author split, and confirmation samples for S04 before disclosing results.
inputs: S02's English corpus, records, and manifest
R01 inclusion decisions, structure, word and sentence implementations, and tags indexed by S01
Fixed specification and settings
acceptance_criteria: Verify the earlier inclusion decisions, newer English-language IDs, observed counts for all 60 cells, and exclusion reasons against the original inputs.

Connected components based on authors and nonempty exact text matches stay within one D/H partition. Report unknown authors, component sizes, and support by cell. Pass near-duplicate groups spanning the partitions to S04 diagnostics.
Keep X02 and automated-definition samples separate. Lock slots, selections, salts, shortfalls, and text hashes by D/H partition.
Check small examples covering the six metrics' denominators and NA treatment where they differ from Phase 1, lexical boundaries, bold projection, weighting, and bootstrap.
steps: Resolve paths from the accepted runs and save settings and input hashes. Select the common UTC months and record exceptions such as unknown dates in the ledger with reasons.

Use separate article ID namespaces for the earlier CC and newer API data. Merge only unique known numeric author IDs across routes. Check cohort counts by year and month and missing authors, tags, edited_at, retrieval times, and capture times.
Build nonempty exact-match word sequences from fixed S and P/L ordering. Assign D/H by fixed SHA-256 parity of the smallest key in each connected author component. Keep H lexical comparisons sealed.

For X02 calibration, select 2 earlier slots per year-month and 10 newer slots per month. For confirmation, select 12 and 30 respectively. Use the fixed salt and one article per author. Separately select 50 calibration and 100 confirmation articles per route, excluding the X02 samples. Isolate the mapping between IDs and blind IDs.

Import the fixed word and sentence rules. Use small synthetic fixtures to check apostrophes, Unicode and URLs, fragments, P/L, bold spans, zeros and NA, weights, and insufficient support for intervals.
pitfalls: Lock the specification in S03 and keep H results sealed.
Use separate numeric article ID namespaces for each route. Identify individuals by their numeric author IDs, excluding handles and organization IDs.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the cohort, D/H assignments, settings, samples, and tests to S04. Check input hashes and disclosure history on resumption.

tasks.title: Run the calculations and independent assessments against the fixed specification
tasks.goal: Calculate the six core metrics, vocabulary, X01–X03, and C01 on the fixed cohort. Save support, uncertainty, and verification evidence.
inputs: Cohort, settings, D/H assignments, samples, and tests sealed by S03
Original inputs and fixed extraction, word, and sentence implementations referenced by the S03 manifest
acceptance_criteria: Trace original data, settings, code, environment, D/H, samples, and dictionaries by hash. Seal D selections and classifications before opening H.
Map the six M metrics to every article. Output calculations, support, intervals, and failure reasons for all V01/V02 candidates, the five fixed V03 series, X01–X03, and C01.

Retain two independent AI assessments for X02 and the automated-definition verification records. Positive spans, manual counts, missing values, and unknowns are verifiable. Identify slots with insufficient sample support.

Independently reproduce the handling of 5,000 replicates, the 4,750 valid-replicate requirement, Holm/BH, zero denominators, required months, and each fixed sensitivity. List all comparison keys and check coverage and original values.
steps: Verify the S03 hashes and synthetic fixtures. Apply the earlier word, sentence, and bold projection rules to the new data and reuse the canonical intermediate values for the earlier data. Keep denominators for P sentences and P+L distinct. Record each article's M01–M06 values, numerators, denominators, reasons, and positions.

Use only D to apply V01's same-period rules of 20 occurrences, 10 authors, a maximum author share of 0.20, and fixed ranking. Apply V02's rules of earlier R≤1%, newer R≥2%, 20 newer authors, share≤0.10, and newer F≥0.05/1000. Cap V01 at 200 and V02 at 100. Apply the fixed V03 queries to all five series. Seal the classifications, X01 dictionary, and validation sample before checking all candidates on H.

Classify candidate X01 5-grams on D. The primary dictionary includes general explanation entries with no exclusion flags. Within each H period, divide the union of matching word positions for phrases used by at least two other authors by W_B. For X03, test the fixed 5 opening and 8 closing expressions in the first and last 50 words respectively, with the close as primary. Keep headings, overlaps in short articles, and shared signatures as supplementary outputs.

Use the S03 blind IDs to assign X02 and the separate automated-definition sample to two independent AI assessment streams. Save reviewer, packet, evidence, and original response, and seal both streams before either sees the other. Label E and G separately for each sentence. Record disagreements, indeterminate cases, word-rate bounds, agreement and κ, and required cells. Mark checks without a reference as unverified.

Produce F/R/A, D/H counts, NA, separate exploration for unknown authors, and complete yearly and monthly tables. Distinguish primary values, sensitivity estimates, near-duplicate groups, topic support and excluded mass, 200-word windows, and tag exclusions. Keep separate V01 and V02 rows for shared terms and apply BH once to the union of hypotheses.

Resample author clusters with PCG64 and the fixed seed. Record the monthly and earlier-year weights, per-replicate C01 regression and pooled SD, extrapolation backtests, and the family covered by each correction. Save the comparison index, independent arithmetic and interval readback, and rerun commands.
pitfalls: Keep years, months, candidates, samples, and thresholds fixed even when results are weak.
Record failures to meet accuracy thresholds and processing failures separately. Use separate evidence for computational checks and content validity.
C01 is a descriptive extrapolation of four earlier annual means. The author bootstrap quantifies variation across author clusters, leaving changes in year-level structure outside its scope.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the sealed comparisons, diagnostics, and independent readback to S05. On resumption, check the most recent verified checkpoint and the input, dictionary, and assessment hashes.

tasks.title: Verify the arithmetic and scope of claims for 18 items
tasks.goal: Determine what the measurements and comparisons support using the saved values. Make decisions and evidence traceable.
inputs: S04 comparisons, article values, assessments, denominators, diagnostics, and independent readback
S03 cohort, settings, samples, and input hashes
acceptance_criteria: Retain exactly 18 decisions covering the six M metrics, V01/V02, five V03 series, X01, X02 E/G, X03, and C01. Link them to all comparison keys and fixed sensitivities.
Provide values, denominators, uncertainty, content verification, alternative explanations, and permissible wording for each decision. Give reasons for NA and unknown values.
Retain X02 fixed-sample differences and bounds due to unknown labels, unmet V02 criteria, all 24 quality comparisons, and the six C01 metrics and backtests.
Have an independent reviewer check the saved values against the wording. Save findings, corrections, and verification of corrections. Completion requires checking every item and saving its decision.
steps: Check the cohort manifest and all comparison keys. Distinguish reused S04 recalculations from checks performed at this stage. Extract denominators, monthly support, valid replicates, corrections, and NA reasons from the saved comparisons.

Join all fixed sensitivity rows and distinguish direction, changes in population, insufficient support, and inapplicability. Keep the quality sample's baseline, display-error, advertising, and signature comparisons across all six M metrics, with reasons.

Check for consensus references, manual segmentation count differences, bold provenance, and positive and negative support for V03, X01, and X03. For each of E and G in the fixed X02 sample, check presence, word rate, assessable counts, agreement and κ, and the uncertainty range due to unknown labels.

Check F/R/A, raw author counts, Q, and unmet replication conditions for V. For C01, check the four-point extrapolation on the original scale, out-of-domain values, backtests, and sensitivities. Identify remaining differences in acquisition, survival, editing, and topic composition.

Use evidence to assign each of the 18 items limited acceptance, hold, or indeterminate. Distinguish observed automated values from measurement validity. Record permissible wording and evidence locations for every item. Have a separate reviewer verify the evidence and wording.
pitfalls: The original run's 2 limited acceptances, 14 holds, and 2 indeterminate decisions are historical. Assign the new run's decisions from its own evidence.
Rerun the full calculation and bootstrap only to investigate a specific discrepancy that the existing checks cannot resolve.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the 18 decision rows and references to saved values to S06. On resumption, verify the manifest and evidence locally against the original records.

tasks.title: Compile the comparisons and four supplementary materials
tasks.goal: Link numbers, figures, examples, and claims to the underlying comparisons so readers can verify the scope and limitations.
inputs: S05's 18 decisions, fixed sensitivities, evidence-index, and independent checks
S04 comparisons, candidates, yearly and monthly tables, stored article values, and X02 assessments
S03 cohort and saved tags
acceptance_criteria: Retain the 18 decisions and all fixed candidates. Index prose, tables, figures, and examples with denominators and sources, and link them to the saved comparisons.
Build the four November 16 resources under the fixed conditions. Independently verify row counts, cohorts, missingness, units, and saved values.
Show the product of article prevalence and the mean among positive articles, the years without observations, tag missingness, and the definition of AI tags.
Verify HTML rendering, search, and links on the actual output. Record any areas that could not be verified and whether the optional November 23 work was performed.
steps: Copy S05's permissible wording to an 18-row claim ledger and link the values and evidence. Provide entry points for the 11 questions. Let readers find the cohort, distribution, yearly results, sensitivities, and X02 E/G combinations through the text, figures, and tables.

Preserve all fixed candidate rows, F/R/A comparisons by condition, yearly and monthly tables, and necessary examples with sources. Base the classifications on sealed D contexts. Quote only what is needed and avoid presenting examples as AI authorship judgments.

Build four resources from saved values for the nine comparison conditions, M05/M06 prevalence and amount among users, yearly general explanatory expressions, and saved tag composition. Keep full tables and summaries separately. Index each table's checks, source rows, and rerun commands.

Make the cohort periods, denominators, points versus percentage points, reasons for NA, and remaining differences in acquisition, measurement, and composition easy to find. Independently check chart values, year axes, descriptions, search, and links.

If the November 23 supplement is explicitly requested, save formatting by tag and the fixed 24-article HTML presence check in separate derived files. Preserve original data, main calculations, candidates, and formal decisions.
pitfalls: The comparison uses a fixed observed corpus. Treat topic and AI authorship as unknown when the only evidence is a missing tag, and avoid treating the whole corpus as classified technical articles.
The supplementary materials describe the fixed observed corpus. Purchasing, publication, final manuscript approval, and measurement accuracy are outside their scope.
tasks.resume_instructions: Pass the 18 decisions and materials to the root-level summary. Verify that the index opens the relevant tables and evidence in the distribution and the run output.
